the renaissance club.location: North Berwick, East Lothian, Scotland (Firth of Forth coast)
the renaissance club.style: Coastal links built on fast fescue with firm, running ground and full exposure to sea air. Plays shorter on the card than the yardage suggests when conditions firm up.
event_notes: 2026 Genesis Scottish Open reverted to the routing used at the 2019 debut: the first seven holes of each nine largely swap, while holes 8, 9, 17, and 18 stay the same.
The stadium par-3 formerly played as hole 6 is now hole 15, rebranded as The Thistle, with expanded grandstand capacity for a louder Sunday finish.
Hole 16 no longer plays as a par-5 (it was reachable in prior years). The closing four holes now run drivable par-4, short par-3, long par-4, long par-3, finishing par-4.

key_holes.note: Front-nine par-5 scoring opportunity when wind cooperates.
Back-nine par-5 and the longest hole on the card.
Drivable par-4 with the right wind. Birdie-or-bust off the tee.
The Thistle stadium hole. Short but bunkered and exposed to crowd energy.
Demanding par-4 that replaced a former par-5. Pot bunkers right demand precision off the tee.
Long par-3 closer where club selection and wind matter late in the round.
Finishing par-4 back toward the clubhouse. Bogeys are common under Sunday pressure.

the renaissance club.weather_notes: Scottish summer weeks often bring mild temperatures and wind that stays under 15 mph, but intermittent showers can soften fairways and change approach spin.
